title: Clarification of Treatment of Electronic Sales of Livestock Act of 2016
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was reported to the House on September 20, 2016. The summary of that version is repeated here.)

Clarification of Treatment of Electronic Sales of Livestock Act of 2016

(Sec. 2) This bill amends the Packers and Stockyards Act, 1921 to expand the definition of "marketing agency" to include any person who engages in the business of buying or selling livestock, on a commission or other fee basis, through the use of online, video, or other electronic methods. The term "marketing agency" does not include a person whose annual average of online, video, or electronic sales of livestock, on a commission or other fee basis, is less than $250,000.

(Sec. 3) The bill also permits electronic funds transfers and other expeditious payment methods that the Department of Agriculture determines to be appropriate to be used as options for meeting prompt payment requirements for livestock purchases.

summary.headline: This law updates the Packers and Stockyards Act so online and electronic livestock sales are clearly covered as marketing agency activity, with a $250,000 annual threshold, and allows electronic payment methods for prompt payment.
summary.what_it_does: The law changes the definition of "marketing agency" in the Packers and Stockyards Act of 1921 to include anyone who buys or sells livestock for a commission or fee using online, video, or other electronic methods. It exempts anyone whose average yearly electronic livestock sales on a commission or fee basis are under $250,000. It also allows the Department of Agriculture to accept electronic funds transfers and other quick payment methods as ways to meet the prompt payment rules for livestock purchases.

who_it_affects.group: Livestock marketing agencies that sell animals online or by video on a commission or fee basis
who_it_affects.how: They are treated as covered marketing agencies under the Packers and Stockyards Act if their average annual electronic sales exceed $250,000.

who_it_affects.group: Small electronic livestock sellers with average annual electronic sales under $250,000
who_it_affects.how: They are not counted as marketing agencies under this definition, so they fall outside this part of the Act.

who_it_affects.group: Livestock buyers and sellers who use electronic payment systems
who_it_affects.how: Electronic funds transfers and other fast payment methods approved by the Department of Agriculture can be used to meet prompt payment requirements for livestock purchases.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The law took effect when it was enacted on October 7, 2016, though the Department of Agriculture's decisions about which payment methods count are made separately.
